main_text.l: eium & mollicies. Multam enim malitiam
docet ociofitas, Ecclesi.33.Ezechiel.16.2.Re-
gum 11. Item, contubernia & colloquia ho-
minum impudicorum, Proverb.7. Ecclesi.
42.Corrumpunt enim bonos mores, collo-
quia prava,1. Corint.15.Et vetus dictum est,
Si juxta claudum habitaveris, discès & ipse
claudicare. Dina filia Iacob, non continet se
domi suæ, sed evagatur ad alienas mulieres:
itaque amittit suam pudicitiam, Genef.34.
Præterea oculorum jactus, Ecclesi.9. Iob.31.
auditus obscoenarum cantilenarum, conta-
ctus externus, impura lectio, & occasio, &c.
Tertium remedium est, ut homo elonget-
se ab igne luxuriæ, i.à præsentia mulieris, cu-
ius species gladius igneus est, teste Hieron.
Hoc remedium docet Paulus 1. Corinth. 6.
inquiens: Fugite scortationem. Hoc usus est
Joseph, Genef. 39. Item Antiochus tertius,
qui cum Dianæ sacerdotem vidisset supra
modum eleganti forma, continuo solvit E-
phesio[?], veritus ne vis amoris aliquid ipsum
facere compelleret, quod phas non esset. At
Israelitæ conveniunt cum filiabus Moab.
quare primum scortantur cum eis, deinde
abducuntur ab ipsis in idolatriam. Et statim
sequitur supplicium, quia multa millia in-
terficiuntur, Num.25.
Quæritur autem cur fugiendo pugnan-
dum sit cum hoc peccato, & cur non possit
aliter melius vinci, quàm hac ratione, quem-
admodum Ambrosius dicit? Responsio: Quia

page.notes: Page starts mid-sentence: the first word "eium" is a fragment and may be the end of a word such as "ocium"; left as printed. The first line of the page does not carry a clear running head beyond "NVPTIALES.", which is given as NUPTIALES. The word "Ephesio" is printed "Ephefo" and is uncertain. "Regum 11." is printed with two numeral characters; read as printed. The long s is rendered as plain s throughout. "Quia" is underlined in the print; the underline is not reproduced. The line "Ecclesi.9." and the reference numbers are copied as printed.
